articles.title: Storm-2603 Hackers Exploit SharePoint ToolShell Flaws to Hide Fileless Backdoor and Launch Ransomware Attack
articles.summary:
A China-linked threat group tracked as Storm-2603 has used the SharePoint ToolShell flaws to plant a backdoor that never touches the disk. The group then tried to run Warlock ransomware on the same network. The break-in hit an on-premises SharePoint server and ended with a ransomware launch that security software blocked. articles.title: ARTEX AI Hacking Framework Found on 1,465 Public Servers, Some Hosting Cyberattack Tools
articles.summary:
Security researchers have found ARTEX, an AI-powered penetration-testing framework, exposed on 1,465 internet-facing hosts. Some servers also hosted command-and-control tools, phishing software, and exploit files, showing how automated security-testing platforms are appearing alongside established attack infrastructure. articles.title: Claude Dispatch Flaw Lets Malicious Browser Extensions Run Code on Connected Computers
articles.summary:
A flaw in Anthropic’s Claude Dispatch let a malicious browser extension run commands on a computer via Claude Desktop. That computer could even be a different machine signed into the same Claude account. articles.title: Hackers Could Bypass ChatGPT Lockdown Mode to Steal Conversations Without Users Knowing
articles.summary:
A flaw in ChatGPT let attackers slip past Lockdown Mode, the safety setting meant to stop data leaks. Check Point Research found that a hidden pop-up trick could copy a user’s full chat history, show fake windows, and push malware.
